article.title: Why a High Retention Rate Can Hide Customer Downgrades
article.why: Distinguish customer survival from value retention.

paragraphs.en:
A high retention rate sounds reassuring. If 90 percent of customers remain active from one year to the next, management may conclude that the customer base is healthy. But retention answers only one question: did the customer stay? It does not tell us whether the customer kept the same value.

Imagine a loyalty program where 90 percent of members are retained. Among those retained customers, however, many move from a high rank to a lower rank. Others visit less often, spend less per trip, or stop buying important categories. The company still counts them as retained, but the commercial relationship has weakened.

This matters because binary retention can hide value migration. A customer who spent 300,000 yen last year and 80,000 yen this year is ‘retained’ if the definition only requires one purchase. From a customer-value perspective, however, that is a substantial decline. The same problem occurs when an active customer shifts from weekly visits to one visit every two months.

A better framework separates customer survival from customer quality. First, measure whether customers remain active. Second, measure how retained customers change in spending, frequency, rank, category breadth, and margin. A transition matrix can show movement from high, medium, and low value states across years.

Cohort analysis is useful because it keeps the starting population fixed. For example, take customers who were Gold members in 2025 and follow where they are in 2026: still Gold, upgraded, downgraded, or inactive. This avoids confusing customer movement with changes in the overall population.

Retention should also be paired with revenue retention. Customer retention counts people; revenue retention tracks how much value remains. A business may retain 90 percent of customers but only 75 percent of prior-year revenue from that cohort. That tells a different story.

The opposite pattern is possible too. A company may lose some low-value customers while retained customers become more engaged, producing lower customer retention but stronger revenue retention. Whether that is good or bad depends on strategy and acquisition cost.

For loyalty programs, rank retention is another useful metric. If most top-tier members remain members but fall to lower tiers, the program may have a hidden downgrade problem. Looking only at ‘active versus inactive’ will miss it.

The practical lesson is simple: retention is not the same as stability. When reporting retention, ask what happened to the value of the customers who stayed. A healthy customer base is not merely one in which people remain present; it is one in which important relationships remain economically strong.

This distinction also affects campaign evaluation. Suppose a retention campaign prevents customers from becoming completely inactive, but those customers continue to reduce spending. The campaign may improve the binary retention rate without creating enough incremental revenue to cover its cost. Analysts should therefore define the desired behavior before choosing the KPI.

One useful dashboard separates four layers: customer retention, spend retention, rank transition, and engagement change. Customer retention shows how many people remain. Spend retention shows how much prior value remains. Rank transition reveals upward or downward movement. Engagement measures such as purchase frequency or category breadth show whether the relationship is becoming richer or thinner.

Segmenting the result can uncover further risks. A stable overall retention rate may hide deterioration among younger customers, high-value customers, or customers using a particular channel. If one segment improves while another worsens, the average may barely move.

Definitions also need consistency. A customer counted as retained after one small transaction is different from a customer counted as retained only after reaching a minimum activity threshold. Changing that definition between years can create artificial improvement or decline.

So a strong retention report should state both the rule and the quality measures behind it. Instead of saying only ‘Retention is 90%,’ it can say, ‘90% remained active, but 18% of retained customers moved down at least one value tier and cohort revenue retention was 82%.’ That wording makes hidden downgrades visible and gives management a clearer basis for action.
paragraphs.zh:
高 retention rate 很容易讓人安心。例如90%的顧客從去年到今年仍 active，管理層可能認為 customer base 很健康。但 retention 只回答「顧客有沒有留下」，並沒有回答「留下的人是否維持相同價值」。

例如 loyalty program 的 retention 是90%，但其中很多 retained customers 從高 rank 掉到低 rank，來店頻率下降、每次消費降低，或不再購買重要 category。公司仍把他們算成 retained，但商業關係已變弱。

Binary retention 因此會掩蓋 value migration。某顧客去年消費30萬日圓、今年只消費8萬，只要定義是「至少買一次」，他仍然被算作 retained；從 customer value 看卻是大幅下降。

較好的框架應拆成 customer survival 與 customer quality。先看顧客是否還 active，再看留下的人在 spending、frequency、rank、category breadth、margin 上怎麼變。Transition matrix 可以追蹤 high/medium/low value 的跨年移動。

Cohort analysis 很重要，因為它固定起始 population。例如把2025年 Gold 會員固定下來，觀察2026年仍為 Gold、升級、降級或 inactive。這樣不會把 population change 誤認成 customer movement。

Retention 也應搭配 revenue retention。Customer retention 計算人數，revenue retention 看 cohort 留下多少價值。90%的顧客留下，但 cohort revenue 只保留75%，故事就完全不同。

反過來也可能發生：流失一些低價值客，但 retained customers 更活躍，因此 customer retention 較低、revenue retention 卻更強。是否是好事要看 strategy 與 acquisition cost。

對會員制度而言，rank retention 也很重要。高階會員雖然還在，但大量掉 rank，就是 hidden downgrade problem。只看 active/inactive 會完全漏掉。

因此 retention 不等於 stability。報 retention 時，還要問留下的人價值如何變化。健康的 customer base 不只是在場的人多，也要看重要關係是否仍然有經濟價值。

Campaign evaluation 同樣受影響。若 retention campaign 只是阻止 inactive，卻沒阻止 spend 持續下降，binary retention 可能變好，但 incremental revenue 未必足以 cover cost。

Dashboard 可以拆成 customer retention、spend retention、rank transition、engagement change 四層，再配合 segment 檢查。

最後，retention definition 必須固定。一次小額交易也算 retained，和必須達最低活動門檻才算 retained，是完全不同的 KPI。好的報告應把 rule 與 quality measures 一起呈現，例如「90%仍 active，但18%的 retained customers 至少掉一級，cohort revenue retention 82%」。
paragraphs.ja:
高いretention rateは安心材料に見えます。例えば90％の顧客が翌年もactiveなら、customer baseは健全だと考えたくなります。しかしretentionが答えるのは「残ったか」であり、「同じ価値を維持したか」ではありません。

loyalty programで90％がretainedでも、その中で高rankから低rankへ落ちる顧客、来店頻度が下がる顧客、一回当たり利用額や重要category利用が減る顧客が多ければ、関係は弱くなっています。

binary retentionはvalue migrationを隠します。前年30万円使い当年8万円しか使わなくても、1回購入すればretainedと定義される場合があります。customer valueの観点では大幅低下です。

より良いframeworkはcustomer survivalとcustomer qualityを分けます。activeかどうかに加え、spending、frequency、rank、category breadth、marginの変化を見ます。transition matrixでhigh/medium/low valueの移動を追えます。

cohort analysisではstarting populationを固定できます。2025年Gold会員を追い、2026年にGold維持、upgrade、downgrade、inactiveのどこへ移ったかを見ることで、population changeとcustomer movementを分けられます。

retentionにはrevenue retentionも組み合わせます。customer retentionが90％でもcohort revenue retentionが75％なら、価値は大きく減っています。逆に低価値顧客が一部離脱し、残った顧客のvalueが上がる場合もあります。

rank retentionも重要です。top-tier会員が会員として残っても低rankへ大量に落ちればhidden downgradeです。active/inactiveだけでは見えません。

したがってretentionはstabilityと同じではありません。残った顧客の価値がどう変わったかを確認する必要があります。

campaign評価でも、inactive化は防げてもspend低下が続けば、binary retentionは改善してもincremental revenueがcostを上回らない可能性があります。

dashboardはcustomer retention、spend retention、rank transition、engagement changeに分け、segment別に見るとよいでしょう。

retention definitionも固定が必要です。1回の小額購入でretainedとするか、最低activity thresholdを要求するかでKPIは変わります。報告ではruleとquality measureを一緒に示すのが安全です。

vocabulary.usage: Compare customer retention with revenue retention.
Measure engagement change among retained customers.

business.term: Retention tells us whether customers stayed, not whether their value stayed.
